case_notes.content:
Session Type: Initial Intake & Action Plan Alignment

Briefcase & Gate Updates:
- Gate 2 (Housing): Participant successfully stuck to a budget with his partner. He is paying his overdue light bill today so his family can move back into their apartment (currently staying with his mother for stability).
- Gate 2 (Transportation): The 2004 Mercedes E320 is being towed to a shop tomorrow for an oil change and diagnosis. Participant has support from family for rides in the interim.
- Gate 4 (Education/Referrals): Clarified the difference between Voc Rehab and GED. Participant has an upcoming appointment with Voc Rehab (Nov 3/4). He prefers to wait to pursue his GED until after completing Turn90 due to childcare and his partner's work schedule.

CBT & Risky Situations:
- Participant reported a risky situation on Monday (an argument with his partner made him late to Turn90). He successfully identified "breathing" and pausing before reacting as his new coping mechanism.
- Participant processed deep frustrations regarding family dynamics (feeling put in a "man box" by his mother and feeling used by his father). CM validated these feelings and discussed setting healthy boundaries.

Next Steps:
- Complete the tow/repair estimate for the Mercedes.
- Attend the Voc Rehab appointment on Nov 3/4.
- CM provided a reference sheet for a free GED program when participant is ready.

case_notes.note_type: Behavioral incident – disruption, conflict, or left early
case_notes.content:
Charlie arrived late for Q1 this morning, stating that he and his girlfriend had gotten into an argument. He was also late returning from lunch, attributing the delay to being stuck in traffic.

DiYoung and I met with Charlie to address his ongoing attendance concerns. During the discussion, we explained that he has been late four times within the three weeks he has been in the program. Although Charlie provided an explanation for each incident, we emphasized the importance of consistent attendance and punctuality as expectations of the program.

Charlie was informed that he is expected to maintain perfect attendance and arrive on time for all scheduled activities during the remaining five weeks of the program. We explained that continued attendance issues will result in his transition back to Resource Navigation to focus on establishing greater stability before continuing with the program.

Below is a record of Charlie's tardiness:

10/28: Arrived late for Q1 and Lab Block.

10/27: Arrived late for Lab Block.

10/21: Arrived late for Q1.

case_notes.content:
Session Type: Initial Intake & Action Plan Alignment (Note: CM reviewed existing goals, indicating some prior contact, but session functioned as a foundational Action Plan review). 

[Client] reported successfully creating a budget plan with his partner to catch up on bills. We reviewed his 90-day Action Plan goals: obtaining his GED and entering an auto-mechanic program. 

Briefcase & Stability Check: The primary barrier to [Client]'s GED enrollment is transportation. Currently, the household shares one vehicle, requiring [Client] to wake up 4 hours early to transport his partner and mother to work. [Client] is currently working on repairing his own vehicle (2004 Mercedes E320) which is currently at a local Euro mechanic awaiting diagnosis. 

CBT/Skills practiced: Discussed recognizing triggers for 'moving too fast' (impulsivity) and practicing taking a step back. Explored setting boundaries with negative coworkers and utilizing the same boundary-setting skills with his mother regarding parenting his children. 

Action Step for next week: [Client] will follow up with the mechanic to get a diagnosis/quote on his vehicle to regain independent transportation.

case_notes.content: Client] identified 90-day goals including catching up on bills, securing reliable transportation (fixing current car or getting a new one), and restarting their clothing brand. Education goals include obtaining a GED, as [Client] completed up to the 11th grade and requires math and history credits. The GED will enable enrollment in an auto mechanics vocational program and serve as a positive example for [Client]'s children. Explored CBT themes, identifying 'moving too fast' (impulsivity) as a past behavior leading to negative consequences. Discussed workplace triggers such as disrespect, politics, or lack of knowledge, and practiced strategies for maintaining boundaries. CM will assist [Client] with GED program online enrollment. A personal mantra was established: 'Where there is no support, I create some.'

Participant: Charlie Graham
Age: 27
Date of Birth: January 5, 1999

Intake/Case Management Summary:
Charlie Graham participated in an initial case management intake and motivational interview. Charlie reported that his previous involvement with the criminal justice system has been limited to county jail and driving-related charges. He reported that he was incarcerated in 2024 following an incident involving taking his mother’s vehicle. Charlie identified marijuana as his only current substance-use concern. When asked whether he could currently pass a drug screen, he stated that he would not be able to pass due to marijuana use.

Motivational Interviewing/Assessment:
Charlie expressed dissatisfaction with the current direction of his life and stated that he recognizes the need for new options and a different route moving forward. He identified vocational training as one of his primary goals and expressed interest in developing skills that could provide him with better opportunities. Charlie acknowledged that he is currently taking risks that could negatively affect his future and recognized the importance of making different decisions.

Charlie reported having some existing support, including the mother of his two children, who assists him with transportation. He also reported currently having a place to stay. Charlie expressed some concern about what the program may be able to offer him and asked questions regarding available opportunities and resources.

Strengths:

* Recognizes that his current direction needs to change.
* Expressed interest in vocational training.
* Has housing at this time.
* Has transportation support from the mother of his children.
* Demonstrated willingness to discuss his marijuana use and barriers to program participation.
* Expressed openness to considering new options.

Barriers:

* Currently unable to pass a drug screen due to marijuana use.
* Transportation depends partly on outside support.
* Limited previous involvement with structured vocational opportunities.
* Expressed uncertainty regarding his next steps and available options.

Goals:

1. Work toward being able to pass the program’s drug screen requirements.
2. Explore vocational training opportunities.
3. Identify healthier and more productive options for moving forward.
4. Develop greater stability and direction in his personal and professional life.
5. Reduce behaviors that could place his future at risk.

Intervention:
Staff used motivational interviewing techniques to explore Charlie’s current circumstances, goals, barriers, and readiness for change. Charlie was encouraged to identify the direction he wants his life to take and consider what changes may be necessary to reach his goals. Staff discussed the importance of working toward meeting program requirements, including the ability to pass a drug screen.

Plan/Next Steps:
Orientation is set for October 12 at 3 o’clock
Charlie and staff agreed to schedule his program orientation approximately two weeks out. Prior to orientation, Charlie will work toward addressing his marijuana use and becoming eligible to meet the program’s drug-screen requirement. Staff will continue to assess his readiness for participation, vocational goals, and resource needs during the next contact.
